subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 3: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
central_question: How can understanding food diversity, nutrients, food tests and responsible choices help us build a balanced diet and a healthy body?
in_scope_units: What we eat — recording weekly food choices and recognising variety
Food in different regions — links among crops, soil, climate, taste, culture and traditions
Changes in cooking or culinary practices over time
Components of food — carbohydrates, fats and proteins
Vitamins and minerals, their functions, sources and deficiency diseases or disorders
Nutrients, protective nutrients, nutrient loss during cooking, roughage and water
Testing food for starch, fats and proteins
Balanced diet and variation in nutritional needs
Comparing packaged foods, junk food, fortification and FSSAI
Food miles, local food, food waste and the farm-to-plate journey
banned_topics: Detailed digestion and the human digestive system
Cellular respiration and biochemical energy pathways
Medical diagnosis or treatment beyond the chapter's advice to consult a doctor

known_pitfalls.claim: A food item contains only one nutrient.
known_pitfalls.correction: A food item may contain multiple nutrients; peanuts, for example, show both proteins and fats.

known_pitfalls.claim: All carbohydrates turn blue-black with iodine.
known_pitfalls.correction: Iodine gives a blue-black colour with starch, which is one type of carbohydrate; sugar is a carbohydrate but not starch.

known_pitfalls.claim: Roughage is a nutrient that supplies energy.
known_pitfalls.correction: Roughage does not provide nutrients or energy, but it is essential for smooth passage of stools.

known_pitfalls.claim: A balanced diet is identical for every person.
known_pitfalls.correction: Nutritional needs vary with age, gender, physical activity, health status and lifestyle.

recommended_example_progression: Connect personal food records, regional crops and changing culinary practices.
Reason from symptoms to nutrient deficiencies using the James Lind and iodised-salt cases.
Interpret starch, fat and protein tests from observations.
Evaluate a balanced diet and packaged-food labels.
Connect millets, food miles, local food and responsible eating.
